english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, you attempted to **(..SPECIFY CONDUCT..) which you were prohibited from doing by a restraining order made under

(A)_[section 360 of the Sentencing Act 2020,]_
(B)_[section 5 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997,]_

imposed by **(..SPECIFY COURT..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE OF ISSUE OF RESTRAINING ORDER..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981 and section 363(1) and (2) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Note – this offence applies to breaches of orders made under section 5 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 and section 360 of the Sentencing Act 2020. For the offence relating to breach of an order made under section 5 of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 applying before the Sentencing Act 2020 was brought in force on the 1st December 2020, see offence H7653.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates' court, see section 363(2)(a) of the Sentencing Act 2020 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
